transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

My head feels foggy and I can’t focus long enough to figure out my bills or make decisions about work anymore. It's just gotten to the point where I can't think clearly enough to sort anything out on my own.
Did these thinking and decision-making problems start after a head injury, stroke, infection, or another medical illness, or have they been present since childhood or long before any such event?

No, I've never had a head injury, a stroke, or any big medical illness, and I didn't have these problems when I was a kid. It really just started up recently after my hours got cut at work and the stress about my bills got so bad.

Have these concentration and decision-making problems caused only mild difficulty, or have they become severe enough that you can no longer manage your daily activities, work, or finances on your own?

It's really severe, and I can't manage any of it on my own anymore. I've already missed work shifts, fallen behind on my rent, and stopped seeing my friends entirely. Now I just lie around the apartment all day, completely exhausted and worrying about money.
Have you also noticed problems with memory, attention, or planning that are mild and mostly just make things harder, or are they severe enough that you cannot manage everyday tasks independently?

They are definitely severe enough that I can't manage everyday tasks on my own. My brain feels so foggy that I can't even read a simple form or figure out my bills, which has caused me to miss work shifts and fall behind on my rent.
Did these symptoms begin within a few months of the work and money stress, and have they lasted less than 6 months so far?

Yeah, this really bad up-and-down pattern with the high spell and then this awful crash started about a month ago right after my hours got cut. But before that, I actually had this deep, dragging depression coming and going for several months, though it's gotten a lot worse this past month.
Before the stress about your hours and bills started, had you already been feeling depressed most days for at least two weeks, or did the low mood begin only after that stressor?

Yes, I was already dealing with that deep, dragging depression coming and going for several months before my hours were cut. It definitely started before the work stress, but it has gotten much worse over this past month.
During the times you’ve felt depressed over those months, did the low mood last most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks at a time?

Yes, it did. During those low times, I would just sit in my apartment feeling this heavy, empty sadness almost every single day for weeks on end. It lasted pretty much all day long, and it's only gotten worse over this past month.

Besides the stress about your hours and bills, did you also have several other depression symptoms during those low periods, such as losing interest in things, changes in sleep or appetite, feeling worthless or guilty, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Yes, I completely stopped caring about walking by the lake or building my model cars, and I barely eat to the point where my pants are getting loose. I wake up around three in the morning with my mind racing, constantly telling myself I'm a lazy screwup and feeling like there's just no point to anything anymore.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you would be better off dead?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. I'm just extremely overwhelmed, stressed, and completely exhausted by this whole situation with my bills and work. It just feels like a lot to carry right now.
Have these depressive symptoms made it impossible for you to work, take care of yourself, or manage daily tasks, or are you still able to function with some difficulty?

Yes, they've made it pretty much impossible for me to function. I've already missed several work shifts and fallen behind on my rent because I feel so foggy and drained all the time. I've also stopped seeing my friends entirely and just lie around the apartment all day worrying about money.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a current depressive episode with pervasive low mood, marked anhedonia, reduced appetite/weight loss, early-morning awakening, excessive self-criticism/worthlessness, fatigue, impaired concentration/decision-making, and marked functional impairment affecting work, finances, and social functioning. Symptoms have been present for weeks and worsened over the past month, with no suicidal ideation. The presentation is most consistent with severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms.
